class.name: DirectionalLight3D
class.brief_description: Directional light from a distance, as from the Sun.
class.description: A directional light is a type of [Light3D] node that models an infinite number of parallel rays covering the entire scene. It is used for lights with strong intensity that are located far away from the scene to model sunlight or moonlight. Light is emitted in the -Z direction of the node's global basis. For an unrotated light, this means that the light is emitted forwards, illuminating the front side of a 3D model (see [constant Vector3.FORWARD] and [constant Vector3.MODEL_FRONT]). The position of the node is ignored; only the basis is used to determine light direction.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], shadow detail is sacrificed in exchange for smoother transitions between splits. Enabling shadow blend splitting also has a moderate performance cost. This is ignored when [member directional_shadow_mode] is [constant SHADOW_ORTHOGONAL].

If [code]true[/code], shadows extend past [member directional_shadow_max_distance] out to [member directional_shadow_cache_max_distance], through an extra far cascade whose shadow map is kept from frame to frame instead of being drawn again every frame. Its resolution is set by [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/directional_shadow/cache_size]. The shadow map follows the camera by scrolling: when the camera has moved far enough (see [member directional_shadow_cache_margin]), what the shadow map holds is shifted, and only the strips that came into view are drawn. It is only drawn whole the first time, when the light turns by more than about a degree, when the camera jumps far away, and when the camera's projection or the light's shadow settings change enough to call for it. [b]Note:[/b] Only supported by the Forward+ renderer.

How much larger than the area it has to cover the cached cascade's shadow map is made, which sets how far the camera can move before it scrolls. Higher values make it scroll less often, by larger steps, at the cost of a lower resolution. At [code]1.0[/code], it scrolls whenever the camera moves by a texel.
The distance up to which the cached cascade extends shadows. Only used when greater than [member directional_shadow_max_distance].

If [code]true[/code], each split keeps a cache of the shadows static objects cast into it, kept from frame to frame like the far cascade of [member directional_shadow_cache_enabled]. Every frame, a split starts from a copy of its cache, and only the objects that move or change are drawn over it. Objects count as static once they haven't moved or changed for 30 frames, unless they are skinned, have blend shapes, use materials animated with [code]TIME[/code], use visibility ranges, or have their instances picked on the GPU. Where static objects appear, move, change or go away, the caches are drawn again there. When the camera moves, the caches scroll along with the splits, and only the strips that come into view are drawn. This saves most of the cost of drawing the splits in scenes made mostly of static objects, at the cost of memory: the caches have an atlas of their own, a quarter larger on each side than the directional shadow atlas (see [member ProjectSettings.rendering/lights_and_shadows/directional_shadow/size]). [b]Note:[/b] Only supported by the Forward+ renderer. Only the first viewport drawn in a frame uses the caches; the others draw the splits whole.

The cached cascade's shadow map is drawn again a band of rows at a time, one band every frame, so that objects that move show up in it. This is the number of frames a full sweep of it takes: lower values make moving objects' shadows follow sooner, higher values cost less per frame. At [code]0[/code], it is never drawn again on its own, which suits scenes where nothing moves that far away.

Proportion of [member directional_shadow_max_distance] at which point the shadow starts to fade. At [member directional_shadow_max_distance], the shadow will disappear. The default value is a balance between smooth fading and distant shadow visibility. If the camera moves fast and the [member directional_shadow_max_distance] is low, consider lowering [member directional_shadow_fade_start] below [code]0.8[/code] to make shadow transitions less noticeable. On the other hand, if you tuned [member directional_shadow_max_distance] to cover the entire scene, you can set [member directional_shadow_fade_start] to [code]1.0[/code] to prevent the shadow from fading in the distance (it will suddenly cut off instead).

The maximum distance for shadow splits. Increasing this value will make directional shadows visible from further away, at the cost of lower overall shadow detail and performance (since more objects need to be included in the directional shadow rendering).

Sets the size of the directional shadow pancake. The pancake offsets the start of the shadow's camera frustum to provide a higher effective depth resolution for the shadow. However, a high pancake size can cause artifacts in the shadows of large objects that are close to the edge of the frustum. Reducing the pancake size can help. Setting the size to [code]0[/code] turns off the pancaking effect.

The distance from camera to shadow split 1. Relative to [member directional_shadow_max_distance]. Only used when [member directional_shadow_mode] is [constant SHADOW_PARALLEL_2_SPLITS] or [constant SHADOW_PARALLEL_4_SPLITS].
The distance from shadow split 1 to split 2. Relative to [member directional_shadow_max_distance]. Only used when [member directional_shadow_mode] is [constant SHADOW_PARALLEL_4_SPLITS].
The distance from shadow split 2 to split 3. Relative to [member directional_shadow_max_distance]. Only used when [member directional_shadow_mode] is [constant SHADOW_PARALLEL_4_SPLITS].
Whether this [DirectionalLight3D] is visible in the sky, in the scene, or both in the sky and in the scene.

constants.constant: Renders the entire scene's shadow map from an orthogonal point of view. This is the fastest directional shadow mode. May result in blurrier shadows on close objects.

Splits the view frustum in 2 areas, each with its own shadow map. This shadow mode is a compromise between [constant SHADOW_ORTHOGONAL] and [constant SHADOW_PARALLEL_4_SPLITS] in terms of performance.
Splits the view frustum in 4 areas, each with its own shadow map. This is the slowest directional shadow mode.
Makes the light visible in both scene lighting and sky rendering.
Makes the light visible in scene lighting only (including direct lighting and global illumination). When using this mode, the light will not be visible from sky shaders.

Makes the light visible to sky shaders only. When using this mode the light will not cast light into the scene (either through direct lighting or through global illumination), but can be accessed through sky shaders. This can be useful, for example, when you want to control sky effects without illuminating the scene (during a night cycle, for example).
